newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SOCIAL SECURITY CHANGES TO BE REVIEWED - PM.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SOCIAL SECURITY CHANGES TO BE REVIEWED - PM.

text.p: The Hungarian government will review its recent social security contribution changes after the end of March, Prime Minister Gyula Horn said on Wednesday.
"At the end of the first quarter (of this year), we will review the effects of the steps instituted and will alter them as necessary," he told a Hungarian television show.

The government lifted the exemption of certain small businesses and one-person corporations from having to pay social security taxes as of January 1, 1997, in an effort to help close the gapping social security deficit.
The IMF late last year warned Hungary that changes will have to be made in social security financing in order not to repeat the deficit of 1996.
Last year the social security's shortfall ballooned to 73 billion forints against a planned 17.8 billion, mainly because of lower-than-planned contributions.

Horn declined to say how the social security scheme might be altered but told the TV programme that many government experts have suggested further-reaching changes than what was taken by the government.
The PM also said that social security remains the Achilles' heal of Hungarian fiscal reform.
"The deficit is huge and the problems are enormous," he said. -- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 40 40
